intro: School psychologists assess students and solve complex problems with families. The closest of the 25 careers below is special education teaching at the secondary level, with an 83% match, while Genetic Counselors are 81% matched and earn a BLS May 2025 median of $100,040, or 4% more than the $95,990 school psychologists earn.
why_it_works: Your work means testing students, interpreting results and building plans with teachers and parents who may disagree. O*NET rates social perceptiveness at 4.25 out of 5 for this job, and judgment and complex problem solving at 4. Teaching, counseling and therapy roles use the same skills. Every match needs no more education than you already have. The gaps are budgets and operations.
tips: School administration pays $105,870, which is 10% more, and builds on your work with staff.
College teaching in psychology is an 82% match; health specialties teaching pays $107,310.
Speech-Language Pathologists earn $97,870, about the same, but need their own license.

faq.q: What jobs can former school psychologists do?
faq.a: The closest matches are secondary special education teachers (83%), Marriage and Family Therapists (82%) and postsecondary psychology teachers (82%), based on O*NET 31.0. Genetic Counselors are 81% matched and earn $100,040, which is 4% more than the $95,990 school psychologist median.

faq.q: Which careers for school psychologists pay more?
faq.a: 9 of the 25 matches pay more. Postsecondary law teachers earn $128,500 (34% more), health specialties teachers $107,310 (12% more) and school administrators below the college level $105,870 (10% more), according to BLS May 2025 data. Administration builds directly on work with school staff.

faq.q: Do school psychologists need another degree?
faq.a: Not more education in general: all 25 matches need no more than school psychologists already have. Many roles in this group expect a professional certification or license, so check the requirements for each new field before you apply, especially in therapy and counseling.

faq.q: What skills should school psychologists build?
faq.a: The skills that most often need work are managing materials, managing financial resources, operations analysis and instructing. Service orientation already rates 3.88 out of 5 for this job in O*NET, so running programs and budgets is the main step toward administration.
